instruction.text: Listen to each person by tapping on their picture and match the pieces of information accordingly.

cats.sound: My schedule is packed, and by the time I get home I just want something quick and easy. Most of my meals come from takeaways, frozen foods, or ready‑made meals from the supermarket. It’s not exactly glamorous, but it saves me time and energy during busy weeks. And different from what many might think, premade meals can be cheaper than cooking fresh. Still, I know that processed food is not the most healthy, so I'm hoping to find better options.

Cooking is where I feel most creative. I love trying recipes from different cuisines. I'm currently experimenting with French dishes. Unlike baking, cooking lets me improvise. I’ll taste as I go, add extra spices, or swap ingredients depending on what I have. It’s a fun way to explore the world without leaving my kitchen, and every meal feels like a little adventure.

I’ve always preferred baking to cooking. There’s something calming about the structure of it. Recipes in baking feel precise and dependable—if you measure carefully and follow the steps, the result is usually exactly what you expect. I enjoy taking the time to weigh ingredients, mix the batter just right, and wait while something slowly rises in the oven. It feels almost like a small science experiment that rewards patience with something warm and delicious at the end.

atoms.sound: During a busy day, cooking is too time-consuming and tiring.
It is difficult to eat healthy with processed food.
Cooking fresh can be more expensive than buying ready-made dishes.
Learning new cuisines and trying out new dishes is exciting.
It feels easier to improvise when cooking rather than when baking.
Cooking is a creative process, where you can easily try new things.
The baking process feels calming and dependable.
Baking is a complex process, almost like a proper experiment.
The long wait during the process makes the delicious outcome at the end even more rewarding.
